story: Alaska DNR's Final Finding and Decision on ADL 234762, signed November 10th, conveys about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA at no cost, down from 19,500 acres in the July preliminary decision

claims.claim: Alaska DNR published the public notice of its Final Finding and Decision on ADL 234762 on November 10th.
claims.verbatim: Publish Date: 11/10/2026
claims.source_outlet: State of Alaska Online Public Notices
claims.notes: WebFetch on 2026-11-11 returned the title, Publish Date 11/10/2026 and Archive Date 12/12/2026. The showrunner's headless-Chromium transcript at out/2026-11-10/src/notice_text.txt matches it.

claims.claim: DNR's final decision conveys approximately 6,800 acres of state land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: convey approximately 6,800 acres (subject parcel) of State-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA) through a noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 1, Executive Summary. Read from the rendered page image of the showrunner's download of this URL, since the PDF is a scan with no text layer. Corroborated by the Beacon ('approximately 6,800 acres of land for free') and the notice page. The four legal-description parcels (C12 to C15) add up to 6,801.30 acres.

claims.claim: DNR cut the conveyance from 19,500 acres in the preliminary decision to approximately 6,800 acres.
claims.verbatim: DNR has determined that it is appropriate to reduce the conveyance acreage from 19,500 to approximately 6,800 acres
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 1. The same document is not consistent. Pages 17, 19, 23, 24, 25, 29 and 31 say 'approximately 20,000 acres', and the WSWCD summary on pages 19 and 20 says 19,950, the figure earlier runs used. The Beacon and the Sentinel both say 19,500. Use 19,500, which is the FFD's own headline figure. The cut is 65.1 percent (12,700 of 19,500), not the Sentinel's 70 percent.

claims.claim: The preliminary decision on the AIDEA conveyance was dated July 10th.
claims.verbatim: This Final Finding and Decision (FFD) complements, updates, and modifies the Preliminary Decision (PD) dated July 10, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 1. Background date, labeled as such.

claims.claim: DNR Commissioner John Crowther signed the final decision.
claims.verbatim: Approved by: John Crowther Commissioner Department of Natural Resources State of Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 32, signature block with a handwritten signature.

claims.claim: The final decision is dated November 10th.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 32. The date is handwritten next to the signature and matches the notice publish date in C01.

claims.claim: The transfer is a noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance under AS 38.05.810(a)(1).
claims.verbatim: The conveyance will be a noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance pursuant to Alaska Statute (AS) 38.05.810(a)(1) (Public and Charitable Use)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 2.

claims.claim: DNR requires no appraisal because the conveyance is at no cost.
claims.verbatim: As a no-cost conveyance, no appraisal is required.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 10, Stipulation 5. The 'no cost' part is corroborated by the Beacon ('for free').

claims.claim: The parcel lies approximately two miles north of Houston, within Township 18 North.
claims.verbatim: approximately two miles north of Houston in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, within Township 18 North Seward Meridian
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 2. The notice page says the same.

claims.claim: AIDEA proposes to use the land for a multi-use industrial and energy development district.
claims.value: multi-use industrial and energy development district
claims.verbatim: AIDEA proposes to use the conveyed land to establish a multi-use industrial and energy development district for the public purpose and public interest of creating jobs, improving energy reliability, and diversifying the economy.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 1. The Beacon quotes the same sentence.

claims.claim: The signed decision names creating jobs, improving energy reliability and diversifying the economy as the public purpose.
claims.value: creating jobs, improving energy reliability, and diversifying the economy
claims.verbatim: It is in the best interest of the State to convey the land to AIDEA for the public purpose of creating jobs, improving energy reliability, and diversifying the economy.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 32, Section VIII Final Finding and Decision.

claims.claim: The first parcel in the legal description is 1,320 acres, on a plat approved April 2nd, 1917.
claims.verbatim: according to the plat approved by the U.S. Surveyor General's Office in Juneau, Alaska, on April 2, 1917, containing 1,320 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 4. T18N R3W, Sections 9, 10 and 11.

claims.claim: The second parcel is approximately 3,560 acres of Tract A, on a BLM plat accepted April 9th, 1963.
claims.verbatim: according to the plat accepted by the United States Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management in Washington D.C., on April 9, 1963, containing approximately 3,560 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 4. Portion of Tract A, T18N R2W. This is the largest of the four parcels.

claims.claim: The third parcel is approximately 1,441.30 acres, on a plat approved April 2nd, 1917.
claims.verbatim: according to the plat approved by the U.S. Surveyor General's Office in Juneau, Alaska on April 2, 1917, containing approximately 1,441.30 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 5. T18N R3W, Sections 1 to 4.

claims.claim: The fourth parcel is approximately 480 acres, on a plat approved December 4th, 1915.
claims.verbatim: according to the plat approved by the U.S. Surveyor General's Office in Juneau, Alaska on December 4, 1915, containing approximately 480 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 5. S1/2 and NE1/4 of Section 13, T18N R3W. Check on the total: 1,320 + 3,560 + 1,441.30 + 480 = 6,801.30 acres. Do not confuse this 480-acre parcel with the separate 480-acre Mike Peacock Experimental Forest, which the parcel adjoins (FFD page 19).

claims.claim: The southern edge of the parcel sits about half a mile from the north bank of the Little Susitna River.
claims.verbatim: The southern extent of the subject parcel is located approximately one half mile from the north bank of the Little Susitna River
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 5. The same sentence continues that the western extent is about two miles from the George Parks Highway.

claims.claim: DNR redrew the parcel to avoid any overlap with the Haessler-Norris trail system.
claims.verbatim: DNR has modified the size and location of the subject parcel being conveyed to AIDEA to avoid any overlap with the Haessler-Norris trail system.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 13. Page 5 says the northern boundary was 'adjusted to the south along aliquot parts to avoid overlapping the Haessler-Norris Trail System', and page 17 says the reduced area was drawn to 'completely bypass' it.

claims.claim: DNR says AIDEA intends to keep allowing public access to the parcel until a patent is issued.
claims.value: prior to issuance of a patent
claims.verbatim: DNR has been informed that AIDEA intends to continue to allow public access to the subject parcel prior to issuance of a patent
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 13. The next clause says AIDEA 'will maintain the authority to determine which specific activities will be allowed'. This is DNR reporting AIDEA's stated intent, not a binding stipulation. The Sentinel describes 'a provision allowing the public to use established trails on the parcel.'
claims.suggested_phrasing: According to DNR, AIDEA intends to keep public access open until the patent issues, while AIDEA decides which activities are allowed.

claims.claim: The Division of Forestry and Fire Protection applied for a public easement along Zero Lake Road on October 2nd.
claims.verbatim: contingent on the approval of the pending application for a public easement that was submitted by the Division of Forestry and Fire Protection (DFFP) on October 2, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 5. Page 8 gives the same date, and page 7 says the conveyance 'is subject to the public easement application'. Page 8 also says parts of Zero Lake Road (ADL 131, ADL 230731) 'may not constitute legal public access', which is why the easement is being formalized.

claims.claim: DFFP has invested in 23.9 miles of active, inactive and planned forestry roads within the parcel.
claims.verbatim: DFFP has invested in the construction of 23.9 miles of active, inactive, and planned forestry roads.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 5, describing the secondary dirt roads within the final subject parcel. Do not mix this with C38's 29 miles, which is DFFP's figure for the larger PD project area.

claims.claim: The decision identifies three anadromous waters within or bordering the parcel.
claims.verbatim: Waters within or bordering the subject parcel that have been identified as anadromous include: 1. AWC 247-41-10100-2287 2. AWC 247-41-10100-2285 3. AWC 247-41-10100-2231-3050
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 7. These include the unnamed outlet of Bench Lake. Page 14 says the redrawn parcel avoids other anadromous waters such as Deception Creek. The Sentinel's article does not mention salmon streams.

claims.claim: Development on the parcel must stay 100 feet back from all anadromous waters.
claims.verbatim: Development within the subject parcel is also subject to a building setback of 100 feet landward from all anadromous waters
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 9, repeated on page 14. Page 9 also says area-wide planning calls for riparian buffers of 100 to 150 feet, and up to 300 feet after ADF&G consultation.

claims.claim: AIDEA must survey the land and complete all pre-patent requirements within 10 years or the decision becomes void.
claims.verbatim: a condition requiring AIDEA to survey the land and complete all pre-patent requirements within 10 years of this decision, or this decision will be void
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 2, restated in Stipulation 5 on page 10. The 10-year clock applies to survey and pre-patent paperwork, not to development. The Sentinel's 'return to the state if it is not developed within 10 years' runs this together with the separate reversionary interest (C26, C27). See killed.

claims.claim: If the 10-year conditions are not met, AIDEA's rights are extinguished and the parcel reverts to general state land.
claims.verbatim: Any rights or preferences conferred to AIDEA by this decision are extinguished and the parcel reverts to general state land and subject to general DNR management.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 10, Stipulation 5.

claims.claim: The July preliminary decision had waived the state's reversionary interest.
claims.verbatim: In the PD, DNR determined that waiver of the reversionary interest for this conveyance to AIDEA was in the public interest on a preliminary basis.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 12. Corroborated by the Beacon, which says DNR chose to 'reverse the elimination of the reversion clause.'

claims.claim: The final decision no longer waives the reversionary interest.
claims.verbatim: After a review of comments received from agencies and the public, DNR will no longer waive AS 38.05.810(g)'s reversionary interest.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 12. Page 2 says the patent will carry 'a reversionary clause in the patent consistent with AS 38.05.810(g)'. Corroborated by the Beacon.

claims.claim: Land not developed for the purpose described in AIDEA's development plan will revert to state ownership.
claims.verbatim: With this reversionary interest, lands not developed for the intended purpose described in the development plan will revert to general state ownership
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 12. No deadline for development appears in the reversionary language I read.

claims.claim: A related area plan amendment moves approximately 6,152 acres into a new Settlement unit, H-33.
claims.verbatim: DNR is amending the SSAP by removing approximately 6,152 acres of land from units P-01, H-06, U-01, and U-22 to create a new unit, H-33.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 2, repeated on page 6. The land classification order reclassifies 'approximately 6,150 acres', and the amendment is SC-08-001A04. The figure is below 6,800 because units H-07 and H-09 are already classified Settlement (page 6). At the PD stage, WSWCD described the reclassification as about 15,100 acres.

claims.claim: DNR plans to close the parcel to new mineral entry.
claims.verbatim: DNR plans to close the subject parcel to new mineral entry.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 2. The notice page names Mineral Order No. 1330. Page 2 also says there are no current mining claims within the parcel.

claims.claim: Active gas leases lie within the parcel, and the conveyance is subject to them.
claims.verbatim: There are active gas leases within the subject parcel that this conveyance will be subject to.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 2. The number of leases is not given.

claims.claim: The preliminary decision was posted for public notice from July 10th to September 14th.
claims.verbatim: Posted under State of Alaska Online Public Notice from July 10, 2026 to September 14, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 15. The comment period was originally set to end on August 19th and was extended that day (pages 15 and 30).

claims.claim: DNR describes the comment period as an extended 67 days.
claims.verbatim: DNR exceeded the statutory requirements of AS 38.05.945 by engaging in an extended public comment period of 67 days (July 10, 2026 to September 14, 2026)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 28. Check: July 10th to September 14th is 66 days elapsed, or 67 counting both ends, so DNR's figure is consistent. WSWCD had criticized the original period as 40 days (page 20).

claims.claim: DNR mailed notice to 278 landowners whose property borders the parcel.
claims.verbatim: Mailed notification to 278 landowners with property bordering the subject parcel
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 15.

claims.claim: DNR received eight comments from agencies.
claims.verbatim: DNR received eight comments from agencies and 2,306 comments from the public during the public comment period.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 16.

claims.claim: DNR received 2,306 comments from the public.
claims.verbatim: DNR received eight comments from agencies and 2,306 comments from the public during the public comment period.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 16, repeated on page 23. Corroborated by the Beacon ('more than 2,300 public comments on the transfer, mostly in opposition') and the Sentinel ('more than 2,300 members of the public'). The FFD itself gives no count of comments for or against.

claims.claim: DNR held two virtual public information meetings with an AIDEA representative, on August 27th and September 2nd.
claims.verbatim: These meetings were held on August 27, 2026 and on September 2, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 30. The preceding sentence describes them as 'two virtual public information meetings with a representative from AIDEA'.

claims.claim: The state geological survey said the region has a very high seismic hazard because it is close to the Castle Mountain fault.
claims.verbatim: The region has a very high seismic hazard due to proximity to the Castle Mountain fault, which is capable of producing significant earthquakes.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 18, in DNR's summary of the DGGS comment. In reply, DNR says on page 19 that 'the conveyance does not authorize specific development.' Attribute this to DGGS, not to DNR.
claims.suggested_phrasing: The state's Division of Geological and Geophysical Surveys flagged a very high seismic hazard from the nearby Castle Mountain fault.

claims.claim: The Division of Forestry and Fire Protection identified about 5.5 million board feet of potential timber in units of the original project area.
claims.verbatim: Recent Five-Year Schedules of Timber Sales identify approximately 5.5 million board feet of potential timber volume within units U-01, H-06, P-02, and P-03
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 19, DFFP's comment on the PD. It describes the larger July footprint, not the final 6,800 acres. DNR says it then removed most planned timber and firewood sale areas (page 14).
claims.suggested_phrasing: In comments on the July plan, state foresters counted about 5.5 million board feet of scheduled timber in the affected units.

claims.claim: DFFP said it built and maintains about 29 miles of existing and planned forest roads within the original project area.
claims.verbatim: DFFP has constructed and maintained approximately 29 miles of existing and planned forest roads within the project area
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 19, DFFP's comment on the PD footprint. Compare C20's 23.9 miles inside the final parcel. The two figures have different scopes, so neither contradicts the other. Page 19 also says these roads reach roughly 3,978 acres of Forest-classified land staying with the state, and that the area adjoins the 480-acre Mike Peacock Experimental Forest.

claims.claim: The Senate Resources Committee commented on the preliminary decision on August 19th and September 9th.
claims.verbatim: On August 19, 2026 and September 9, 2026, the Senate Resources Committee commented on the PD.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 21.

claims.claim: The committee's September 9th comment included a seven-page Legal Services memorandum.
claims.verbatim: Their September 9, 2026 comment included a seven-page memorandum prepared by Legal Services.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 21. The next sentence says the comments and memo 'question the legality of the proposed conveyance'.

claims.claim: Senate Resources argued the preliminary decision failed to consider the potential harms of data center development.
claims.verbatim: The preliminary decision failed to consider "many of the potential negative consequences that populations and the environment endure from development of data centers
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 21, in DNR's summary of the committee's comments. The words inside the quotation marks are the committee's own. DNR replied that 'the statute itself rather than 11 AAC 98.010 was the primary legal basis' for its analysis (page 22) and that the conveyance complies with Article IX, section 6.
claims.suggested_phrasing: The Senate Resources Committee argued, in DNR's summary of its comments, that the July plan ignored the potential harms of data center development.

claims.claim: DNR received numerous comments opposing the conveyance for potential data center development.
claims.verbatim: DNR received numerous comments expressing general opposition to the proposed noncompetitive conveyance of approximately 20,000 acres of public land to AIDEA for potential development of data centers and related industrial infrastructure.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 23. This is the first category in DNR's summary, which it orders by frequency (page 23). Note the '20,000 acres' rounding.

claims.claim: DNR acknowledged public concern over the prospect of scalable data center facilities.
claims.verbatim: particularly with respect to the overall acreage and potential future industrial development, including the prospect of scalable data center facilities.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 23, DNR Response. Correction to the brief: the page says 'prospect of scalable data center facilities', not 'potential for'. The Beacon reports that AIDEA listed 'scalable data centers' among possible uses in July.

claims.claim: Commenters warned that data center cooling could deplete aquifers, lower residential wells and threaten salmon streams.
claims.verbatim: Data centers are seen as especially problematic due to their high levels of water usage for cooling, which could deplete aquifers, lower residential well levels, and threaten salmon streams and wetlands.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 25. This is DNR's summary of what commenters said, not a DNR finding.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Commenters, as DNR summarized them, warned that data center cooling could draw down aquifers and wells.

claims.claim: DNR responded that the conveyance does not approve any specific development project.
claims.value: does not approve any specific development project
claims.verbatim: The conveyance does not approve any specific development project.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 25, DNR Response to the environmental and water comments. Similar wording appears on page 19 ('does not authorize specific development') and page 24 ('does not constitute approval of any specific construction or infrastructure').

claims.claim: Commenters raised concern that the development would strain the existing electrical grid.
claims.verbatim: DNR received comments expressing concern that the proposed development would place substantial strain on the existing electrical grid
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 26. The same paragraph records fears that data center load 'could increase rates, reduce reliability, or contribute to power outages.'

claims.claim: DNR said the conveyance does not authorize construction of roads, utilities or transmission facilities.
claims.verbatim: The conveyance itself does not authorize the construction of roads, utilities, transmission facilities, or other associated improvements.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 26, DNR Response to the energy and infrastructure comments.

claims.claim: The remaining 12,700 acres from the July plan stay under DNR management.
claims.verbatim: The remaining 12,700 acres of land identified in the PD will continue to be managed by DNR for other State purposes consistent with the management intent detailed in the SSAP.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 26. Check: 19,500 minus 6,800 is 12,700, consistent with C03.

claims.claim: DNR wrote that it does not need to consider speculative impacts of post-conveyance development.
claims.verbatim: DNR does not need to consider speculative impacts, like those related to the success or specifics of post-conveyance development opportunities.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 27, in reply to the economic-impact comments. Page 12 says the same thing in legal terms: 'DNR's REDOIL review does not need to consider future and speculative impacts.'

claims.claim: A request for reconsideration must reach the Commissioner's Office within 20 calendar days of the decision.
claims.verbatim: Any request for reconsideration must be received by the Commissioner's Office within twenty (20) calendar days after issuance of the decision
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 33. Only people who submitted timely written comment or hearing testimony are eligible. Corroborated by the Beacon ('opens a 20-day window for reconsideration'). My arithmetic, not a claim: 20 days from November 10th is November 30th.

claims.claim: A reconsideration request is considered denied if the Commissioner does not act within 30 days of the decision.
claims.verbatim: If the Commissioner takes no action on a request for reconsideration within thirty (30) days after issuance of the decision, the request for reconsideration is considered denied.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 33. The Sentinel and the Beacon both report the 30 days. My arithmetic, not a sourced claim: 30 days from November 10th is December 10th, three days after the December 7th inauguration. A request must come before any superior court appeal.

claims.claim: Requests for reconsideration carry a fee of $200.
claims.verbatim: Reconsideration must be accompanied by the fee established in 11 AAC 05.160(d)(1)(F), which has been set at $200
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: FFD page 33. Requests may be emailed to dnr.appeals@alaska.gov.

claims.claim: DNR's vicinity map estimates the parcel at 65 percent upland, about 4,370 acres.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: Soil inset ('Approximate Soil Analysis') on the vicinity map, read from the showrunner's downsampled copy at out/2026-11-10/src/vicinity_small.jpg. The same map is FFD page 34. These are soil-data estimates (C56).
claims.suggested_phrasing: DNR's map estimates roughly two thirds of the parcel is upland.

claims.claim: The same map estimates 35 percent of the parcel is wetland, about 2,377 acres.
claims.verbatim: Wetland 35% (2,377)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: Vicinity map soil inset. The inset also shows 'Water 0% (2)'. Check: 4,370 + 2,377 + 2 = 6,749.
claims.suggested_phrasing: DNR's map estimates about a third of the parcel is wetland.

claims.claim: The soil inset totals 6,749 acres and labels its figures as estimates based on soil data.
claims.verbatim: 6,749 total acres, individual acreages next to percentages. *These figures are estimates based on soil data.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.notes: Vicinity map. The 6,749 acres GIS total differs from the 6,800 acres in the decision and the 6,801.30 acres in the legal description. Do not treat the map figure as the conveyance size.

claims.claim: The Alaska Beacon reported more than 2,300 public comments on the transfer, mostly in opposition.
claims.verbatim: DNR received more than 2,300 public comments on the transfer, mostly in opposition.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via The Alaska Current
claims.notes: By James Brooks. Corroborates C35. 'Mostly in opposition' is the Beacon's characterization. The FFD gives no count for or against.
claims.suggested_phrasing: most of them opposed, according to the Alaska Beacon

claims.claim: A former state legislator's lawsuit seeking to block the transfer is still pending, according to the Beacon.
claims.verbatim: That suit is still pending.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via The Alaska Current
claims.notes: The Beacon says 'a former state legislator filed suit to block it' but does not name him. The Sentinel names former Rep. David Eastman (C60). That is two independent outlets. No court docket was fetched.
claims.suggested_phrasing: A lawsuit seeking to block the transfer is still pending, both outlets report.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Sentinel reported the approved transfer covers about 11 square miles, down from more than 30.
claims.verbatim: The approved plan transfers about 11 square miles, down from more than 30 square miles originally proposed.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: By Amy Bushatz. Check: 6,800 acres divided by 640 is 10.6 square miles, and 19,500 divided by 640 is 30.5, so the figures agree with the FFD. The Sentinel does not print 6,800. Its '70%' is killed (see killed).

claims.claim: The Sentinel reported that former state Rep. David Eastman of Meadow Lakes filed the pending lawsuit.
claims.verbatim: A pending lawsuit filed by former state Rep. David Eastman of Meadow Lakes seeks to block the transfer.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Corroborated in part by the Beacon (C58), which describes an unnamed former legislator. Only the Sentinel gives the name.
claims.suggested_phrasing: a lawsuit by former Rep. David Eastman, according to the Mat-Su Sentinel

claims.claim: DNR spokesperson Lorraine Henry said the public comments resulted in significant changes to the decision.
claims.verbatim: These comments have resulted in significant changes to the decision.
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: This was a written statement quoted verbatim by the Sentinel and attributed to 'DNR spokesperson Lorraine Henry said in a statement.' FFD page 4 says the same thing in its own words: 'DNR has significantly modified the PD.'

claims.claim: The winner of the governor's race takes office at noon on December 7th.
claims.verbatim: The winner is set to take office at noon Dec. 7.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: By Eric Stone. Corroborated by the Sentinel ('A new Alaska governor will be sworn in Dec. 7') and ADN, October 27th. The Sentinel's claim that the new governor 'could also take steps to halt or change the transfer' is speculation. If used, attribute it to the Sentinel.

claims.claim: Ranked choice tabulation in Alaska's races begins November 18th.
claims.verbatim: Races begin to be ranked on Nov. 18.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: By Wil Courtney, published November 5th at 8:52 PM AKST. Corroborated by The Alaska Current ('The state also waits until then, Nov. 18, to tabulate ranked-choice votes') and Alaska Public Media, which quotes Wilson on the Nov. 18 tally. No Division of Elections page was fetched.

claims.claim: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins led first choices in the governor's race with 48.99 percent to Bernadette Wilson's 29.13 percent in preliminary results.
claims.verbatim: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, the lone Democrat, holds 48.99% of the vote to Trump-endorsed Bernadette Wilson's 29.13%.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Preliminary results, with about a quarter of ballots outstanding per the KTUU headline. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media on November 3rd ('With 98% of precincts reporting, Kreiss-Tomkins leads with 49% of the vote') and FairVote ('leads with 49.1% of first choices').
claims.suggested_phrasing: Kreiss-Tomkins leads first choices with about 49 percent in preliminary, unofficial results.

claims.claim: FairVote's unofficial, preliminary ranked choice tally shows Kreiss-Tomkins defeating Wilson 55 to 45 percent.
claims.verbatim: In the RCV tally, he defeats Bernadette Wilson 55-45%.
claims.source_outlet: FairVote
claims.notes: FairVote calls it 'This unofficial, preliminary RCV tally' on about 211,000 ballots, with the cast vote record updated November 9th at 3:49 p.m. It says 'there are still more ballots to count, so the results are not final.' FairVote is an RCV advocacy group, so this is a projection and not an official result.
claims.suggested_phrasing: An unofficial preliminary tally by FairVote has Kreiss-Tomkins ahead after rankings.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported that VoteHub called the governor's race for Kreiss-Tomkins.
claims.verbatim: which was enough for VoteHub to call the race in his favor.
claims.source_outlet: The Alaska Current
claims.notes: The headline reads 'JKT wins Alaska's race for governor'. The live-updated article is dated November 3rd and cites results 'posted at 2 a.m. Nov. 4'. This is a media projection, not certification or official RCV tabulation. Do not state that he won as fact.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Kreiss-Tomkins is the projected winner in some outlets, ahead of official tabulation on November 18th.

claims.claim: Commissioner Crowther told ADN in October that approval before the new governor is sworn in was certainly possible.
claims.verbatim: but he said it was "certainly possible" the transfer could be approved before a new governor is sworn in Dec. 7.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, from before the window. By Margaret Carmel, published October 27th. Re-fetched on November 11th. The phrase 'certainly possible' is the reporter's partial quote of Crowther. That article used 'roughly 20,000 acres' and 'more than 2,000 public comments'.

claims.claim: Crypto Briefing reported that Governor Dunleavy announced InvestNorth, described as a state-sponsored infrastructure financing platform.
claims.verbatim: a state-sponsored infrastructure financing platform
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: By Kaye Quema, November 9th. The article attributes it to 'Governor Mike Dunleavy said Monday.' The existence of InvestNorth is corroborated by TechFlow's republication of Bloomberg (Emma Haidar), which says 'a new entity, InvestNorth.' NO PRIMARY FOUND. The gov.alaska.gov newsroom lists only proclamations for November 9th, gov.alaska.gov/press-releases/ returned 404, aidea.org shows nothing on it, and the Bloomberg original returned 403.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Governor Dunleavy on November 9th announced InvestNorth, a state infrastructure investment platform, according to trade press reports.

claims.claim: InvestNorth will use tokenization to digitize ownership interests in infrastructure assets, Crypto Briefing reported.
claims.verbatim: InvestNorth will use tokenization to digitize ownership interests in infrastructure assets.
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: TechFlow's Bloomberg republication says 'Alaska is putting investment contracts on-chain', which corroborates the substance. No primary found.
claims.suggested_phrasing: The platform is reportedly built on tokenized ownership stakes.

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation will operate as an AIDEA subsidiary partnering with digital infrastructure developers, Crypto Briefing reported.
claims.verbatim: Alaska Data Corporation will operate as an AIDEA subsidiary and partner with digital infrastructure developers
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: The article names it 'Alaska Data Corporation LLC (AKDC)'. TechFlow's machine-translated Bloomberg text names 'Alaska Data'. No AIDEA board resolution creating it was found. For comparison, AIDEA's own October 23rd release (C77) covers a different subsidiary, Northstar Fiber.
claims.suggested_phrasing: a new AIDEA subsidiary, Alaska Data Corporation, according to reports

claims.claim: Alaska Data Corporation is meant to help build distributed data centers in communities across the state, according to Crypto Briefing.
claims.verbatim: distributed data centers in communities across the state
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: Single trade-press source for this phrase. The Bloomberg republication does not use it. Keep it attributed. Nothing links AKDC to the Houston parcel, so do not imply a link.
claims.suggested_phrasing: intended, per Crypto Briefing, to back distributed data centers around the state

claims.claim: Brandon Brefczynski, AIDEA's deputy executive director, is president of Alaska Data Corporation, according to Crypto Briefing.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA deputy executive director and president of Alaska Data Corporation
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: Corroborated by TechFlow/Bloomberg, which says 'Brandon Brefczynski, President of Alaska Data and Deputy Director'. That text is machine-translated and calls AIDEA the 'Economic Development Division'.
claims.suggested_phrasing: led by AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski, reports say

claims.claim: Both initiatives were developed with the fintech company Plural, according to Crypto Briefing.
claims.verbatim: The two initiatives were developed in partnership with Plural, a financial technology company serving energy
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: The same page says 'InvestNorth uses AssetOS to coordinate investor commitments, waterfall distributions, transactions'. Corroborated by TechFlow/Bloomberg ('In collaboration with infrastructure financing platform Plural'). plural.com did not resolve for the scouts.
claims.suggested_phrasing: built with the fintech firm Plural, per reports

claims.claim: InvestNorth may offer investment options reserved for Alaska residents, Crypto Briefing reported.
claims.verbatim: investment options specifically reserved for Alaska residents
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: The article says these are subject to securities law, FINRA rules and regulatory approval. TechFlow/Bloomberg says the long-term goal is for 'ordinary Alaskans to directly invest', which is partial corroboration. No dollar amount appears in either source.
claims.suggested_phrasing: some offerings could be limited to Alaska residents, pending regulatory approval, reports say

claims.claim: Crypto Briefing quoted Governor Dunleavy saying Alaska has shown it can manage its resources well for all its people.
claims.verbatim: For decades, Alaska has demonstrated it can manage its resources well for the benefit of all of its people.
claims.source_outlet: Crypto Briefing
claims.notes: Verbatim on the fetched page. It probably comes from a press release that I could not find on gov.alaska.gov. The Dunleavy quotes in the TechFlow republication are machine-translated and are killed.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Dunleavy, as quoted by Crypto Briefing

claims.claim: AIDEA's board voted unanimously on October 21st to form Northstar Fiber Development LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary.
claims.verbatim: voted unanimously to adopt Resolution No. G26-11, authorizing the formation of Northstar Fiber Development LLC, a wholly owned AIDEA subsidiary dedicated to investing in the fiber infrastructure that connects Alaska to the world.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, from before the window. AIDEA press release 20-2026, dated October 23rd. It is the closest primary AIDEA document to the InvestNorth/AKDC news. It does not mention InvestNorth, AKDC or data centers.

claims.claim: The Northstar Fiber resolution authorizes AIDEA to invest up to $75 million in fiber systems.
claims.verbatim: The resolution authorizes investment of up to $75 million in subsea and terrestrial fiber systems, landing stations, backbone and middle-mile networks, and associated capacity
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The same release says 'The resolution only creates the tool; it does not select a particular project, partner, or route.'

claims.claim: Waymo says it will run closed-course evaluations and heavy snowfall data collection in Alaska this season.
claims.verbatim: This season in Alaska, for example, we'll be conducting closed-course evaluations and heavy snowfall data collection
claims.source_outlet: Waymo
claims.notes: Waymo blog post by 'The Waymo Team', November 5th. The blog says Alaska and does not name Fairbanks. Fairbanks comes from FOX Weather (C81) and KTVF (C83).

claims.claim: Waymo's sixth-generation driver uses cameras, radar and lidar.
claims.verbatim: The 6th-generation Waymo Driver uses cameras, radar, and lidar to navigate the world around it
claims.source_outlet: Waymo
claims.notes: A photo caption on the blog reads 'The Ojai and sixth-gen Waymo Driver performing closed course winter testing' but does not say where.

claims.claim: Waymo says its winter testing has logged tens of thousands of real-world miles in Upstate New York, Michigan's Upper Peninsula and the Sierra Nevada.
claims.value: tens of thousands of real-world miles
claims.verbatim: accumulating tens of thousands of real-world miles across Upstate New York, Michigan's Upper Peninsula and the Sierra Nevada
claims.source_outlet: Waymo
claims.notes: These miles are NOT Alaska miles. The scout framing that tied the figure to Alaska is killed.

claims.claim: Governor Dunleavy said there is no better proving ground for winter driving than Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: there is no better proving ground for winter driving than Fairbanks,
claims.source_outlet: FOX Weather
claims.notes: By Kieran Sullivan, November 5th. FOX says Dunleavy posted it on social media, and I did not fetch the original post. The full quote opens 'Alaska has always been a place where innovators come to test their limits,'.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Dunleavy, in a social media post quoted by FOX Weather

claims.claim: Dunleavy said Waymo will test its Ojai and Hyundai IONIQ vehicles in Fairbanks, FOX Weather reported.
claims.verbatim: Dunleavy said Waymo will test its Ojai and Hyundai IONIQ vehicles in
claims.source_outlet: FOX Weather
claims.notes: FOX paraphrases Dunleavy here. Waymo's own blog shows the Ojai in closed-course winter testing but does not mention the IONIQ or Fairbanks. KTVF does not mention vehicle models.
claims.suggested_phrasing: including its Ojai and Hyundai IONIQ vehicles, according to the governor

claims.claim: Waymo told KTVF its Fairbanks work includes manual data collection, supervised autonomous driving and limited structured testing.
claims.verbatim: manual data collection, autonomous driving with a specialist at the wheel, and limited structured testing in Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTVF)
claims.notes: By Alex Bengel, November 10th at 4:27 PM AKST. This is a Waymo statement relayed by the station, and the spokesperson named is Chris Bonelli. It fits Waymo's primary blog (C78). KTVF reports that Waymo did not give vehicle counts, mileage or dates.
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to a Waymo statement to KTVF

claims.claim: Fairbanks Mayor Mindy O'Neall called the testing a great opportunity for Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: I think it's a great opportunity for Fairbanks to be a testing ground.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTVF)
claims.notes: Verbatim on the fetched page. The same story quotes residents who are skeptical, for example Charlie Woolwine: 'I don't think that they're safe and they shouldn't be allowed.' Show both views if either is used.

claims.claim: MEA and Enstar signed a gas exchange agreement involving 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
claims.verbatim: a gas exchange agreement involving 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: MEA release, October 21st (background date). Corroborated by Alaska Public Media on November 6th ('allows Enstar to buy about 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas').

claims.claim: Hilcorp is the third party to the exchange agreement with Enstar and MEA.
claims.verbatim: between Enstar, Matanuska Electric Association and Hilcorp
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: By Ava White. MEA's release title is 'MEA, ENSTAR and Hilcorp Sign Gas Exchange Agreement'. Neither source explains Hilcorp's role.

claims.claim: Enstar must return equivalent gas volumes to MEA no later than March 31st, 2028.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR will return equivalent gas volumes to MEA no later than March 31, 2028.
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: Corroborated by Alaska Public Media ('by March 2028').

claims.claim: MEA expects about $2 million in savings for its members from the exchange between 2027 and 2029.
claims.verbatim: approximately $2 million in estimated savings for MEA members
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: The total breaks down as about $1.3 million in avoided carrying costs plus $700,000 in Cost of Power Adjustment savings over 2027 to 2029. This is MEA's own projection. Alaska Public Media says the same: 'save customers about $2 million between 2027 and 2029'.
claims.suggested_phrasing: MEA projects about $2 million in member savings

claims.claim: Enstar President John Sims called the 1.2 Bcf from Matanuska Electric huge.
claims.verbatim: This 1.2 Bcf that we're getting from Matanuska Electric is huge
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Verbatim quote by a named person on the fetched page. Sims also said 'We don't like to be just in time when we're planning for gas supply, but this is just in time.'

claims.claim: When signed, the exchange agreement was subject to review by the Regulatory Commission of Alaska.
claims.verbatim: submitted by ENSTAR to the Regulatory Commission of Alaska for review
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: MEA says the agreement is 'subject to regulatory approval and implementation', with expedited consideration requested. Only Alaska Public Media reports approval 'in late October', and no RCA order was found, so the approval claim is killed.

stories_surviving: DNR Final Finding and Decision conveys about 6,800 acres near Houston to AIDEA, ADL 234762, November 10th (56 primary claims plus 5 secondary corroborations)
InvestNorth and Alaska Data Corporation announced November 9th (secondary only, hedge throughout, no primary found; AIDEA's Northstar Fiber release is primary background)
Governor's race timing, with RCV tabulation November 18th and inauguration December 7th (preliminary results, hedge)
Waymo winter testing in Fairbanks (Waymo blog primary for Alaska, FOX Weather and KTVF for Fairbanks)
Enstar, MEA and Hilcorp 1.2 Bcf gas exchange (MEA release primary, Alaska Public Media corroborates)

killed.claim: The approved transfer shrinks the parcel by 70% (Mat-Su Sentinel).
killed.why: The primary figures give 1 minus 6,800/19,500, which is 65.1 percent (12,700 of 19,500 acres removed). The Sentinel overstates it. If a share is needed, say 'about two thirds smaller' or 'cut by about 65 percent', derived from C03 and C49.

killed.claim: The land must return to the state if it is not developed within 10 years (Mat-Su Sentinel).
killed.why: This runs two separate provisions together. The FFD's 10-year condition voids the decision if survey and pre-patent requirements are not done (C23, C24). The reversionary interest covers land not developed according to the development plan and has no stated deadline (C26, C27).

killed.claim: The July preliminary decision covered 19,950 acres.
killed.why: The FFD's headline figure is 19,500 (page 1), and the Beacon and Sentinel agree. 19,950 appears only in the WSWCD comment summary and DNR's reply to it (pages 19 and 20). The FFD also rounds to 'approximately 20,000' in several places. Use 19,500.

killed.claim: DNR acknowledged the 'potential for scalable data center facilities'.
killed.why: The brief's wording is not on the page. Page 23 reads 'the prospect of scalable data center facilities'. Replaced by C44 with the correct verbatim.

killed.claim: Waymo has done 'tens of thousands of miles' of winter testing in Alaska.
killed.why: The Waymo blog ties the miles to Upstate New York, Michigan's Upper Peninsula and the Sierra Nevada. For Alaska it promises only closed-course evaluations and snowfall data collection (C78, C80).

killed.claim: Waymo cars were seen charging at the GVEA parking lot in Fairbanks.
killed.why: Single-sourced to KTVF, which relays a GVEA employee's sighting with no direct quote. No second source or primary.

killed.claim: Waymo's Fairbanks fleet size, mileage and testing dates.
killed.why: Not disclosed. KTVF says Waymo did not answer timeline questions.

killed.claim: Dunleavy quotes in the TechFlow article ('let everyone become a small-scale capitalist', 'This model will take root across the United States', and others).
killed.why: TechFlow is a machine-translated, compiled republication of a paywalled Bloomberg story, and Bloomberg returned 403. The wording is back-translated and is not a verbatim quote by a named person.

killed.claim: InvestNorth terms and investment structures have not been finalized.
killed.why: This appears only in TechFlow's translation of Bloomberg. Crypto Briefing uses conditional language but does not say it. No primary.

killed.claim: Each eligible Alaskan will receive a $1,200 dividend this year, a 3 GW North Slope data center was once planned, and vote counting finishes November 25th (TechFlow).
killed.why: Single-sourced to a machine translation, off-story, and not checked against a primary. The November 25th date also conflicts in kind with the official RCV tabulation date of November 18th.

killed.claim: A governor's office or AIDEA press release announced InvestNorth and AKDC.
killed.why: None found. The gov.alaska.gov newsroom lists only proclamations for November 9th, gov.alaska.gov/press-releases/ returned 404, and the aidea.org homepage shows nothing. AIDEA's latest related release (October 23rd) covers Northstar Fiber only.

killed.claim: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the governor's race.
killed.why: Not official. It rests on a VoteHub projection reported by The Alaska Current. Official RCV tabulation starts November 18th. Used only as an attributed projection (C66).

killed.claim: UA Regents postponed the 'AI Engaged' AI statement of intent to February, or sooner if President Matt Cooper requests it.
killed.why: Single-sourced to KTUU (Alex Bengel, November 9th). alaska.edu, alaska.edu/bor and alaska.edu/news all returned 503. Searches of Alaska Public Media and ADN found no second report. Killed under the single-source rule. Recheck when alaska.edu is back.

killed.claim: UA CTO Benjamin Shier recommended the delay, and Jonathon Taylor described the feedback as 'passionate'.
killed.why: Same single KTUU source, no primary reachable. The tool output also gave Taylor's title inconsistently (it said 'Director of Public Works'), so his title is unverified. One of his quotes contains an em dash and would fail house style anyway.

killed.claim: Enstar aims for 6 to 7 Bcf in storage by the end of December, and the deal lifts its projection to about 5 Bcf.
killed.why: Single-sourced to Alaska Public Media paraphrasing John Sims. No Enstar primary (the enstarnaturalgas.com news page returned 404) and no second outlet.

killed.claim: The RCA approved the Enstar, MEA and Hilcorp exchange in late October.
killed.why: Only Alaska Public Media reports it. MEA's October 21st release says the deal was submitted to the RCA for review, and no RCA order was fetched. C90 is used instead.

killed.claim: Enstar supplies gas to about 150,000 members.
killed.why: Alaska Public Media wording only. Enstar is not a member cooperative, so 'members' is probably a mistake for customers. Not corroborated.

killed.claim: The vicinity map is dated 'Date Printed: October 2026'.
killed.why: I can't read it at the resolution of the available downsampled image or the FFD page 34 scan.

killed.claim: A new governor could halt or change the transfer (Mat-Su Sentinel).
killed.why: Speculative, with no mechanism or statement from the incoming administration. Only usable as the Sentinel's attributed view, and not used as fact.
